title: Paying off debt — avalanche vs snowball
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: If you have several debts, list them with balance, interest rate and minimum payment. Two proven methods: the avalanche method puts every spare rupee on the highest-interest debt while paying minimums on others — it saves the most money. The snowball method clears the smallest balance first for quick wins and motivation — it costs a bit more interest but helps people stay on track. Either beats paying evenly. Credit-card and instant-loan debt usually comes first because of the 30–48% interest. Never miss a minimum payment on any loan, avoid taking new debt to repay old debt unless the new rate is clearly lower, and keep a small buffer so an emergency does not push you back to the card. Talk to your lender early if you cannot pay; ignoring it makes things worse.
summary_hinglish: Saare karz ki list banao (balance, byaj, minimum payment). Avalanche mein sabse zyada byaj wale karz ko pehle chukate hain (sabse zyada paisa bachta hai); snowball mein sabse chhota balance pehle (motivation). Credit card aur instant loan aam taur par pehle. Kisi bhi loan ka minimum payment mat chhodo.
summary_hi: सभी कर्ज़ की सूची बनाएं (बकाया, ब्याज, न्यूनतम भुगतान)। एवलांच तरीके में सबसे ज़्यादा ब्याज वाला कर्ज़ पहले चुकाते हैं (सबसे ज़्यादा बचत), स्नोबॉल में सबसे छोटा बकाया पहले (प्रेरणा)। क्रेडिट कार्ड और इंस्टेंट लोन आम तौर पर पहले। किसी भी लोन का न्यूनतम भुगतान न चूकें।
